There's something indescribably sad about a dystopian Broken Masquerade setting. I have a lot of thoughts about this piece, and I'm not even sure if I relate to the narrator, but the prose is so strong that I can't help but be drawn in.

A "plague of thought" is a malignant being that inhabits your psyche, latches onto your dreams, and sucks them dry. It is an intrusive negative thoughtform fuelled by a cynical, alien Mindscape that knows what you fear and robs your life of its joy. They take innumerable shapes and sizes with a motif of endless, fractal spirals. One can nary identify it until it is too late.

This opening is fascinating to me. When I read it first, it seemed a little on the nose — I guess I've been sort of immunized to cosmic horror speak by this website, haha. But as I read on, I realized that the monsters here are just as terrifying as they should be.

+1, of course. Thanks for posting despite the deadline, haha.

I might be bias due to my love for the Wanderers' Library lol but I love the way this story was told. The way you incorporated the image too - having it be from a photo-clairvoyant friend - was really unique and helped tied in the image with the rest of the story. Agreeing with TrustyOlValet2's comment as well, Lampyra is a relatable character and I also love dream-based entities lmao. Keep up the good work Flops!

I love Serpent's Hand, I love Pattern Screamers, and I love dream-based entities with lots of crosslinks. Furthermore, Lampyra kinda feels like how I'd react to something like this. All around, good jobs, Flops!

item.title: "Scattersomnia": A Disease of the Wise and Drowsy Wanderers
item.content:encoded:
"Scattersomnia": A Disease of the Wise and Drowsy Wanderers
Author: Lt Flops

▷ Entry for DAY ONE ◁

▷ Entry for DAY TWO ◁

This is a Serpent's Hand GOI Format entry for the FINAL DAY of the 144-Hour Jam Contest Two! The theme was "More Than Meets The Eye", and this one was particularly tough to write for. I don't think I had a clue of what I wanted to do until 9:30 PM tonight — less than three hours before the deadline. As a result, this is the quickest I've ever written a draft, and is about the hardest coldpost I'll probably ever post.

As before, the GOI I was focusing on was Oneiroi, and again, this fits in the Broken Masquerade Canon! I took the opportunity here to consolidate a couple of pieces of authorial lore I've held across my writing career on the SCP Wiki:

▷ Authorial Lore

1) The first is the tenuous story of my recurring psychic character Agent Samara Maclear. Samara is a clairvoyant and special attachment on multiple Mobile Task Force units, coming into contact with the likes of SCP-3739, SCP-4190, and SCP-4519 across her frontline career. After her death, she found herself at the black Gates she's always seen in her dreams, but on the wrong side. Where? A place known only as the Monster's Hollow.

2) Actually, this one is something I'm not quite sure I'll reveal. You'll have to figure it out on your own. No spoilers!

In this article, I also made the implicit connection between SCP-2000 and SCP-3002 (written by HammerMaiden and MayD, respectively). These are two articles that I love a lot, and I've headcanoned a connection between the two for a long time.

△ Close

As before, I do want to polish this up after the voting period is complete and the contest proper has finished. Hope you enjoyed!

▷ Special Thanks

Special Thanks — Critters & Beta Readers

NONE — This was a complete coldpost, written (mostly) stream of consciousness!
